stories.title: Dell Launches Unified Semantic Layer, Enterprise Knowledge Graph, and Knowledge Agents for Its AI Data Platform
stories.body: On October 6, 2026, Dell Technologies announced three new additions to its AI Data Platform: a Unified Semantic Layer, an Enterprise Knowledge Graph, and Knowledge Agents—all designed to give enterprise AI agents trusted, governed context from a company's own structured and unstructured data. Dell's framing is direct: most AI pilots stall not because the model is weak but because production requires accurate, governed context at a scale that pilots never test. The Unified Semantic Layer, Enterprise Knowledge Graph, and Knowledge Agents are slated for general availability in the first half of 2027, with Nvidia Nemotron Retriever models powering reasoning inside the Knowledge Agents.
stories.why: This is the clearest infrastructure-layer commitment from a Tier-1 hardware vendor in 2026—and it validates the exact argument Graas makes about context layers being the prerequisite for agents that work in retail. When a prospect asks why their pilot stalled, you can point to Dell acknowledging that 'making data accessible isn't the same as making it usable'—and then show where Graas sits in that architecture today, not in H1 2027.

stories.title: Gartner: Over 40% of Agentic AI Projects Will Be Canceled by 2027 — Data Quality and Vague ROI Are the Top Killers
stories.body: Gartner predicts more than 40% of agentic AI projects will be canceled by the end of 2027, citing escalating costs, unclear business value, and inadequate risk controls as the three primary causes—not model capability. A concurrent Forrester and Anaconda finding shows 88% of pilots never reach production, with the most cited blocker being the absence of pre-agreed success criteria for what 'the agent works' actually means. The MIT NANDA 'GenAI Divide' report adds that 95% of enterprise generative AI pilots produce no measurable P&L impact within six months, and the 5% that do succeed share one trait: they are wired into the company's real operational data.
stories.why: These three converging analyst findings are the most powerful objection-handler in the category right now—they give a Graas seller permission to ask a prospect 'what does success look like for your pilot?' before a competitor does. The data-readiness root cause maps directly to Graas's context-layer and semantic-grounding argument, making this the backbone of any 'why pilots stall' slide in a deck.
stories.source_label: Pasquale Pillitteri / Gartner, Forrester, MIT NANDA synthesis

stories.title: Salesforce Closes $3.6B Acquisition of Fin (Formerly Intercom), Folding Its 76%-Resolution Agent into Agentforce
stories.body: Salesforce completed its $3.6 billion acquisition of Fin—the customer-service AI company formerly known as Intercom—on September 10, 2026, bringing more than 30,000 business customers and Fin's proprietary Apex support model into the Agentforce platform. Fin's AI Agent resolves 76% of support volume without a human across live chat, email, WhatsApp, SMS, phone, and Slack, compared to Agentforce's own reported 62% resolution rate. Salesforce positioned the deal as buying speed-to-deploy: Agentforce is deeply customizable but slow to stand up, while Fin is packaged, pre-trained, and live in days.
stories.why: The competitive landscape for enterprise support agents just consolidated—any retailer or CPG company that is Salesforce-native now has an out-of-the-box agent option at $0.99 per resolution baked into their existing contract conversation. Graas sellers need to be ready to explain what a domain-specific, context-grounded retail agent delivers that a generic, horizontal support agent cannot, because 'we already have Fin through Salesforce' will become a standard objection.

stories.title: BCG Case: CPG Agentic Planning Platform Delivers +2–4% In-Stock Lift, +4–10% Fill Rate, and 40–60% Admin Savings
stories.body: A BCG May 2026 executive perspectives report on supply chain documents a CPG company that deployed a multi-agent planning platform with human-in-the-loop validation across forecast reconciliation, inventory replenishment, order optimization, and S&OP allocation for constrained supply. The deployment produced a 2–4 percentage-point improvement in in-stock rate (driving direct revenue lift), a 4–10% improvement in fill rate, and 40–60% administrative savings, with a +2 percentage-point EBITDA improvement projected from year two onward. The architecture used subagents for rationale tracking and materiality validation, with human analysts making the highest-stakes decisions.
stories.why: This is one of the few publicly documented agentic deployments in CPG with named outcome ranges across in-stock, fill rate, and margin—exactly the proof points a Graas seller needs to anchor an ROI conversation with a supply chain or commercial planning buyer. The human-in-the-loop design and subagent architecture also mirror the context-layer approach Graas advocates, making this a credible third-party reference for why the foundation matters.

stories.title: Sierra, Decagon, Fin, Ada: October 2026 Pricing Reality Check — Decagon Median at $432K, Sierra at Six Figures Before Outcome One
stories.body: A vendor comparison updated October 14, 2026 across Sierra, Decagon, Fin (now Salesforce), and Ada shows Decagon's median contract at $432,750 per year (Vendr data), Sierra's estimated platform fee starting at $150,000 per year before any per-outcome charge, and Ada's lowest published price at $30,000 per year. Fin prices at $0.99 per resolution with seat fees from $29, making it the only player in the group with transparent, volume-scalable economics. The architectural split is stark: Sierra and Decagon are standalone platforms above the help desk; Fin lives inside a CRM; Ada runs a multi-channel layer—and in every case the agent belongs to the vendor, not the customer.
stories.why: Retail and CPG enterprise buyers are increasingly asking 'build vs. buy vs. platform' in the same breath—this pricing map gives a Graas seller a concrete anchor for that conversation, especially where a prospect has received a Decagon or Sierra quote and is weighing it against building on top of an existing CRM. The 'agent belongs to the vendor' framing is a differentiation lever for any solution that grounds the agent in the customer's own data and ontology.
